note: Results about the problem itself (not benchmark numbers). 'Peer-reviewed' = journal or refereed conference; 'Preprint' = not yet refereed as far as the maintainers know. Claims may contain inline LaTeX between dollar signs.

entries.title: A counterexample in stochastic optimum control
entries.claim: An optimal pair exists for every $k$ and $\sigma$; the best linear pair is found in closed form; a two-point nonlinear design beats every linear pair for some parameters; a lower bound on the optimal cost is proved (Theorem 3).

entries.title: Team decision theory and information structures in optimal control problems, Part I
entries.claim: With partially nested information, LQG teams have linear optimal policies. The counterexample is not partially nested.

entries.authors: C. H. Papadimitriou, J. N. Tsitsiklis
entries.title: Intractable problems in control theory
entries.claim: A discrete version of the counterexample is NP-complete.

entries.title: Stochastic teams with nonclassical information revisited: when is an affine law optimal?
entries.claim: Identifies cost structures close to Witsenhausen's for which affine laws are optimal.

entries.title: Information and control: Witsenhausen revisited
entries.venue: Learning, Control and Hybrid Systems, LNCIS 241, 281–293 (Springer)
entries.claim: Quantization-based strategies can beat the best linear strategy by an arbitrarily large factor.

entries.title: Review of the Witsenhausen problem
entries.claim: Reviews the status of the problem forty years on, for the session of the 2008 CDC devoted to the counterexample.

entries.title: Variations on the theme of the Witsenhausen counterexample
entries.claim: A semi-tutorial paper that places the counterexample in a broader class of problems: in some of them linear policies are optimal, in others, including Witsenhausen's, the optimal policies are nonlinear.

entries.title: Witsenhausen's counterexample as assisted interference suppression
entries.venue: Int. J. Systems, Control and Communications 2(1/2/3)
entries.claim: Information-theoretic lower bound valid for every vector length; the asymptotic optimal cost of the vector problem is pinned down within a factor of $2$.

entries.authors: P. Grover, S. Y. Park, A. Sahai
entries.title: The finite-dimensional Witsenhausen counterexample
entries.claim: Lattice strategies are within a constant factor of optimal for all parameters and vector lengths; in the scalar case the gap to the bound is numerically at most a factor of $8$. New sphere-packing lower bound, used here as bound (8).

entries.title: Witsenhausen's counterexample: a view from optimal transport theory
entries.claim: The optimal first controller $f$ is strictly increasing with a real-analytic left inverse, so a piecewise-linear $f$ can be exactly optimal only if it is affine. Their Theorem 4 is a family of lower bounds that includes Witsenhausen’s 1968 bound.

entries.authors: P. Grover, A. B. Wagner, A. Sahai
entries.title: Information embedding and the triple role of control
entries.claim: Asymptotic optimal cost of the vector problem pinned down within a factor of $1.3$. Its Corollary 1 holds for every vector length, so it also bounds the scalar problem; in dimension one it gives the closed-form bound used here as (10).

entries.authors: W. M. McEneaney, S. H. Han
entries.title: Optimization formulation and monotonic solution method for the Witsenhausen problem
entries.venue: Automatica 55, 55–65; first in Proc. IEEE CDC-ECC 2011, 5023–5028 (with A. Liu)
entries.claim: Works with the quantile function of $x_1$ instead of the controller, so that the problem becomes the minimization of a quadratic control cost plus an estimation cost over a function space; the journal version gives a monotonic solution method.

entries.authors: A. A. Kulkarni, T. P. Coleman
entries.title: An optimizer's approach to stochastic control problems with nonclassical information structures
entries.venue: IEEE Trans. Automatic Control 60(4), 937–949; first in Proc. IEEE CDC 2012
entries.claim: Recasts problems with this information structure as optimization over joint distributions and solves convex relaxations of them, whose values are lower bounds. A relaxation built on the data-processing inequality solves the instance of Bansal and Başar (1987) exactly.

entries.title: Slopey quantizers are locally optimal for Witsenhausen's counterexample
entries.venue: Proc. IEEE CDC 2016; journal version: IEEE Trans. Automatic Control 66(7), 3152–3168, 2021; arXiv:1604.03806
entries.claim: Carefully constructed slopey quantizers are locally optimal when $k^2\sigma^2 \le 1$ and $k^2 \le 0.005$ (conference version). The journal version shows that local minima of this form exist and are within a constant factor of the optimal cost. The benchmark has $k^2 = 0.04$, outside the conference version's range.

entries.authors: N. Saldi, S. Yüksel, T. Linder
entries.title: Finite model approximations and asymptotic optimality of quantized policies in decentralized stochastic control
entries.claim: Quantized (finite-model) policies are asymptotically optimal for the counterexample, which justifies grid-based numerics.

entries.title: On the inapproximability of the discrete Witsenhausen problem
entries.claim: For the discrete problem with $n$ initial states, approximating the optimal cost within a factor $n^{2-\varepsilon}$ is NP-hard for every $\varepsilon > 0$.

entries.authors: B. Telsang, S. Djouadi, C. D. Charalambous
entries.title: General decentralized stochastic optimal control via change of measure: applications to the Witsenhausen counterexample
entries.claim: Person-by-person optimal strategies satisfy two coupled nonlinear integral equations; a fixed-point existence argument is sketched.

entries.authors: M. Zhao, M. Le Treust, T. J. Oechtering
entries.title: Low-power optimal strategy for Witsenhausen counterexample
entries.claim: A low-power estimation strategy is first-order optimal as the control power $P \to 0$, and it explains the near-optimal sawtooth shape of $u_1$.

entries.title: The exact boundary of linear optimality in Witsenhausen's counterexample
entries.claim: Optimal policies are either linear or not tame. The paper gives the exact region of parameters where a linear policy is optimal, with an essentially unique closed form there. Everywhere else, the benchmark included, no optimal first-stage policy is definable in any o-minimal expansion of the ordered real field; in particular, none is built from finitely many polynomial pieces.
